# 1 Enoch Chapter 84 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Dreams

---

**1** "Now, my son — I plead with you, I beg you: live righteously and uprightly on this earth. Do it so that when judgment comes, the great final judgment of the whole world will not fall on you; so that you and your descendants will receive mercy forever."

**2** "For our Lord is great — truly great and mighty in his greatness. His glory is immense, his mercy and compassion are immense, and his patience is without limit. He will be with you; he will never abandon you.

**3** But watch your heart, my son — don't hide your sins from God; don't let pride rise up before the Lord; don't do evil in his presence."

**4** Now let me show you, my son Methuselah, everything I saw in my visions — I will recount all of it for you.

**5** Before I married, I had two visions — they were entirely different from each other. I prayed to the Lord about both of them.

**6** Blessed be the Lord — the King of all majesty and glory, who created the entire world, who holds all power over everything. He is the King of kings, God of gods, Lord of lords — over every glorious throne and every kingdom, over all the Watchers and all the angelic Governors. He arranges and orders all things. He gives wisdom to the wise and insight to the perceptive. He gives instruction and strength to all people and rules over everything. This King of kings holds power in heaven and governs the earth below as he pleases —

**7** no one can stand against his power, no one can slip past his will, and no one in his presence can say "No." He is the King, the Lord. No one escapes from him, no one flees his judgment; no one can stand before his majesty.

**8** He created the whole world by his power. He has known everything from eternity, and his power has existed from the very beginning. That is why he recorded everything for us on the heavenly tablets.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 84 is Enoch's prayer of praise — a magnificent Jewish doxology. The threefold title 'King of kings, God of gods, Lord of lords' (v. 6) echoes Dan 2:47; Deut 10:17; Rev 19:16. The prayer closes with the heavenly tablets (v. 8) — the divine record that holds all of history. Enoch's pastoral charge to Methuselah (vv. 1-3) is moving: don't hide your sins, don't be proud, live uprightly.*
